https://www.dw.com/en/us-ecuador-forces-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Jbvb The US military said the people on board were escorted to Ecuador before the vessel was destroyed Image: U.S. Southern Command/SOUTHCOM Advertisement The US military said on Friday it had destroyed an alleged drug trafficking boat in a coordinated operation with Ecuador . In a post on X, US Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) said that its forces intercepted a vessel "operating as a floating refueling station" in the Eastern Pacific. According to SOUTHCOM, the vessel was operating "in support of the Los Choneros violent narco-terrorist organization," referring to one of Ecuador's most powerful criminal gangs, which Washington has designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organization . "Working together with our Ecuadorian partners, our coalition dealt a decisive blow to a narco-terrorist operation responsible for moving significant amounts of drugs through the region," SOUTHCOM said. US, Ecuador combat drug cartels In March, Ecuador joined President Donald Trump's "Shield of the Americas" — a US-led coalition focused on combating drug trafficking across the region. Ecuador's strategic location between Colombia and Peru — the world's two largest producers of cocaine — makes the country a key transit hub for drug-trafficking gangs. The US military launched Operation Southern Spear in September 2025 as part of a fight against drug trafficking in the region. The Trump administration, however, has not presented definitive evidence that the vessels targeted in its operations were carrying or transporting illegal drugs.
